nodes.text: Welcome to the *Wanderer's Rest* — beds, board, news, in whatever order you're hungriest for. Stew's on, fire's fed, and the first rumor's free.

choices.text: Your mother kept this bar before you?
The roads — how are they running?

nodes.text: The big one: Silverfall's Masons broke the *Undercroft seal*. Twenty years shut and now there's a market down there again, they say — and kobolds past the rubble line, which they say quieter. Every third stool in this room has an opinion. Bretta's is the only one worth the wood it's sat on: ask her, not me.

First Road's tame as a barn cat — hedgerows, wayshrines, the odd goblin scout getting above himself. The High Road is the High Road: fine to the Long Meadow, chancy to the Fork, and past *Edda's lamp* you'd best be the kind of trouble things regret finding. The Redmasks work the middle stretch. Travel mornings, travel loud.

Peld swears something big turned over in the millpond twice last month. Garton swears it was Peld's bell. Perl swears the cows have learnt to open her gate, and I *believe* Perl. Small town — our strange stays friendly. The road's strange is another jar entirely.

Mam ran this room thirty years — *Osa*, ask anyone grey enough. When my father passed she said grief needed altitude, kissed the bar, and walked the High Road at sixty. Now she waters caravan mules under Silverfall's wall and writes me once a season to say my stew needs more thyme. She's right. Don't tell her.
Stew, bread, roast, and cake that outsold the sermon last feast-day. Eat something before the road does its arithmetic on you.
Fire's free. Stories cost a listen. Sit long enough and you'll pay double.
